_comment: Quality floors for fbtberger-raft. Both numbers may only go UP -- see the kwatro repository's QUALITY.md. Pitest is pointed at the arithmetic the protocol rests on (Quorum, RaftConfig, storage), not at RaftNode: one mutant there means booting a cluster.
_coverage_note: The floor is 0.80 against a measured 80.9 %. Two things changed on 2026-08-30. First, the report no longer counts protoc output: two thirds of this repository by line count is generated (6287 of 9113 lines), it sat at 30.9 %, and together with the hand-written 81.3 % it produced the 46 % that used to be the headline. That number moved with the size of the .proto files rather than with the tests. Second, the tests stopped sleeping: fixed waits were replaced by conditions and, where the code has an event to signal, by latches on the RPC seam. Measured before: 344 tests, no failures, no skips, and line coverage moving between 4199 and 4214 from run to run. Measured after, over four forced re-runs: 2284, 2285, 2284, 2285 -- a spread of one line. The margin to 0.80 is for that one line and no more; raise it when a run is worth pinning. One thing the margin is for, established on the same day and worth not re-investigating: GrpcTransportServer's requestVote and appendEntries -- ten lines -- are recorded by JaCoCo in some runs and not in others, all-or-nothing, with identical test outcomes. GrpcClusterTrafficTest asserts through a latch that both handlers were reached, and it is green in every run, including the runs where those lines read as uncovered. So the code is exercised deterministically and the MEASUREMENT is not; it happens with only those two tests selected, so it is not interference from the rest of the suite. Cause not established. The floor keeps ten lines of room for it.
